OmaStats 1.8 adds a Power tab that shows where your machine's power goes, puts your discrete GPU's temperature and fan on the Sensors page, and starts new bars with a more useful set of readouts. On hybrid laptops it no longer keeps the NVIDIA card awake.

[Download the complete plugin](https://github.com/crmne/omastats/releases/download/v1.8.0/omastats-v1.8.0.tar.gz), or install it with:

```sh
omarchy plugin add https://github.com/crmne/omastats.git --enable
```

![The Power page showing 256 W, split into CPU and GPU history, with CPU package and RTX 3080 readings, using synthetic demo data](https://github.com/crmne/omastats/releases/download/v1.8.0/omastats-1.8.0-power-dark.png)

## New

- **A Power tab, on every machine.** It shows the machine's total draw and its history, then every reading behind it: CPU package power, the RAPL zones beside it (cores, integrated graphics, memory, Intel's platform zone) when they are readable, each discrete GPU, and a Corsair power supply that reports over USB. The total is measured when something measures the whole machine: the power supply, the battery a laptop runs on, or the platform zone. Otherwise it is the CPU package plus the GPUs, and says so. On a laptop the battery cards follow below. Power takes the Battery tab's place, and the battery readout in the bar opens it. By @crmne.
- **Your GPU's temperature and fan on Sensors.** The GPU ring now shows each discrete card, and NVIDIA cards' temperatures and fans join the Temperature and Fans lists, where you can also pick them for the bar. The fan reads in percent, which is all NVIDIA reports. The Fan row moved off the GPU page. By @crmne.
- **A better bar out of the box.** A new bar shows CPU and GPU as graphs, memory as a ring, network as a graph with its rates, and a ring of disk space used. GPU readouts default to the discrete cards, so a desktop with an APU no longer gets an integrated-GPU readout it did not ask for. A bar you have already styled keeps its look. By @crmne.
- **AMD's VRAM clock on the GPU page.** A "Memory clock" row shows when VRAM is stuck at full speed while idle, which several monitors or a high refresh rate can cause, and which raises idle power. By @crmne; thanks @juldeveloper (#31).
- **History in a few clicks.** The History setting steps through 30 seconds, 1, 2, 4, 5, 10, 15 and 30 minutes, and an hour, instead of 30 seconds at a time: four minutes to an hour now takes five clicks instead of over a hundred. By @crmne; thanks @ardentperf (#30).

![The Sensors page with the RTX 3080's temperature in the GPU ring and its fan in the Fans list, using synthetic demo data](https://github.com/crmne/omastats/releases/download/v1.8.0/omastats-1.8.0-sensors-dark.png)

![The default bar: CPU graph, memory ring, network graph with rates, GPU graph and disk space ring, using synthetic demo data](https://github.com/crmne/omastats/releases/download/v1.8.0/omastats-1.8.0-bar-dark.png)

## Fixed

- **An idle NVIDIA card can sleep again.** OmaStats ran `nvidia-smi` every second as soon as it found an NVIDIA card, which kept a hybrid laptop's GPU awake even with its readout and tab hidden. While a card is allowed to suspend, OmaStats now leaves it alone while it sleeps, showing it as Off, and asks an awake one once per idle period, so it can fall asleep. Cards that never suspend, as on most desktops, update every second as before. By @crmne; thanks @adityamiskin (#33).
- **The GPU on Sensors is the one doing the work.** On a desktop whose display starts on the processor's integrated graphics, the Sensors page and the "GPU" sensor readout showed the integrated GPU instead of the graphics card. By @crmne.
- **Stacked bar labels line up with their graphs.** The vertical letters beside each readout sat a little low. By @enterprise-r (#34).

## Known limitations

- A laptop's NVIDIA card is read once per idle period (about six seconds) while it is allowed to suspend, so its figures update less often than the rest. This was checked with tests, not on a hybrid laptop: please report how it behaves on yours.
- Without a power supply, battery or platform zone to measure the whole machine, the Power total covers the CPU and GPUs only, not fans, drives or the rest of the board.
- CPU power and its RAPL zones on Intel, and on AMD without integrated graphics, need a udev rule that makes `/sys/class/powercap/*/energy_uj` readable.
- Power supply readings cover Corsair's USB-connected supplies (the `corsairpsu` driver) only.
- NVIDIA fans report percent of full speed, not rpm, so they do not count towards the Fans ring's average.
- The process search and color fields take typed text only: there is no paste or text selection.
- GPU process lists from open drivers show only your own processes. An integrated AMD card's own load figure jumps between 0% and 100%, so it can disagree with its process list.
- A mirror, raidz or striped ZFS pool counts against its first data drive only. "All disks" is correct, but picking another drive in the pool shows no space for it.
- A vertical bar with many readouts turned on can run into the bar's center section. Turn off readouts you don't need, or use figure-only looks.
